passages.text: “Mendicants, gods and humans like sights, they love them and enjoy them. But when sights perish, fade away, and cease, gods and humans live in suffering.
passages.note: Suffering when loved things fade and end

passages.text: What others say is happiness the noble ones say is suffering. What others say is suffering the noble ones know as happiness.
passages.note: Questioning what the world calls happiness

passages.text: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicants! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”
passages.note: Don't put off what matters; avoid later regret
